brief: Final demand PPI rose 0.4% in August 2026 from July (5.4% y/y), the earliest read on renewed exogenous cost pressure: oil back near $100/barrel as the U.S.-Iran military conflict reignited, and tariff actions targeting Canadian imports resurfaced. Energy PPI jumped 4.2% m/m and 24.3% y/y, the strongest year-ago energy PPI growth since May 2011 excluding the COVID period, because energy costs are ubiquitous across the economy and feed producers' downstream costs. Goods and services PPI diverged: goods reaccelerated, giving back nearly 60% of the May-July declines, while services rose just 0.1%, the slowest pace since June 2025, though the note expects services to face the upstream energy resurgence in coming months. Core PPI (ex food and energy) decelerated for a second straight month but still ran 4.6% y/y, up from July's 4.3%, and is expected to bounce again later in the year. PNC concludes the resurgence, combined with August's outsized hiring gain, narrows the Fed's room to stay patient on inflation or cut rates.
